verdict.rationale: Angular's first-party docs state directly that it provides fine-grained reactivity based on Angular Signals. That covers declaring reactive state and updating only the dependent code. The community complaints about $digest dirty-checking concern legacy AngularJS, not Signals, so they do not contradict this claim. Missing for 10: in-depth docs on the signal, computed and effect APIs and how dependency tracking limits re-runs, plus independent or hands-on corroboration of Signals' fine-grained update behavior.

support.subject: As a developer, I can declare reactive state and have only the dependent UI code re-run when it changes

citations.quote: Reactive and fast state updates with fine-grained reactivity based on Angular Signals
